## What — Experiment Identity

- **Experiment**: Compare SART against 11 baselines on clean accuracy, robustness, reasoning consistency, and shortcut detection F1 across 3 synthetic benchmarks

## Why — Experiment Purpose

- **Claim addressed**: H1 — SART outperforms all baselines on all metrics

## Analysis

<details>
<summary><strong>Key Findings</strong></summary>

1. **SART achieves best accuracy, robustness, and reasoning on all three datasets.** On Math, near-perfect (98.0%/95.8%) — a +47.8pp robustness gain over the next-best baseline.

2. **Data-removal baselines exhibit extreme cross-task variance.** Influence Filtering ranks second on Causal (83.2%/69.2%) but collapses on Financial (63.4%/23.6%).

3. **SART's advantage scales with task complexity.** The gap grows from Math (+11.2pp) to Financial (+16.8pp) to Causal (+20.0pp robustness), confirming that gradient-based correction is most powerful for multi-feature shortcuts.

</details>

<details>
<summary><strong>Claim Status</strong></summary>

- **H1 status**: Confirmed — SART exceeds the best baseline by +16.5pp accuracy and +40.2pp robustness
- **Without group annotations** (unlike Group DRO) or multiple environments (unlike IRM/V-REx/Fishr)

</details>
